finding: The row-role definition's rationale — "The asymmetry with the `role` rule above is deliberate — `status` has an existing predicate to match and `role` does not" — is false, and the mismatch is observable in a single invocation. finding: §2.1's third bullet defines "a round contributes no rows" partly as "when any line in it fails to parse as JSON", but never exempts blank lines — while every existing NDJSON reader in tp skips them before parsing (countAuditFindings splits on \n, trims, and `continue`s on empty; engine.LoadRoundRows and parseRecordRows do the same). A recorded audit round file is a verbatim byte copy of the operator's results file (recordAuditRoundEntry writes `data` unchanged), so it normally ends in a trailing newline, which yields a final empty line under any split. Read literally, essentially EVERY recorded round contributes no rows: every streak is 0, spec_coverage_clean_rounds is always null, divergence can never fire, and the release ships dead. The zero-row case is not hypothetical — internal/cli/audit_record_test.go records two rounds from a completely empty results file today. §2.2 also contradicts itself under this reading: it lists "the latest round contributes no rows, by any of §2.1's three causes" and "the latest round recorded zero rows" as two DISTINCT states reaching role_streaks == [], and §6 test 9 requires them to be distinguishable (only the first emits an advisory) — impossible if an empty or newline-terminated file is classified as unparseable.

finding: §2.1 justifies its trim-but-don't-case-fold role rule with "`status` has an existing predicate to match and `role` does not". An existing role predicate does exist, and it runs inside the very same parse loop this rule feeds: `rolelessRows.observe` (internal/cli/review_record.go:243-251) treats a row as carrying a role when `row["role"].(string) != ""` — no trimming — and is invoked per row by `countAuditFindings` (internal/cli/audit_record.go:149), the function §2.1 elsewhere cites as the predicate to match byte-for-byte. finding: §2.1 says a round contributes no rows when a line "fails to parse as JSON", but the row rules in the same section address a line's `role` and `status` FIELDS — i.e. they presuppose a JSON object. A line such as `42`, `"text"`, `true` or `[]` parses as JSON and is not an object. The two readings are observably different and point in opposite directions: (a) matching countAuditFindings, which unmarshals into map[string]any and therefore errors on such a line, makes the whole round contribute no rows (advisory fires, every streak resets); (b) a literal "it parsed, so it is a row" reading makes it a row that carries no role and is non-PASS, which feeds unattributed_open and other_roles_open and can make divergence fire. §2.1 explicitly pins the PASS predicate to countAuditFindings byte-for-byte but leaves this shape rule unpinned, so an implementer must guess which of the two the same section intends.

finding: §2.2 makes every `tp audit --status` and `--record` walk the trailing clean segment and read each round's NDJSON, and concedes the walk is long exactly in the state the release detects. That cost is new on the agent-facing path: today `tp audit --status` reads at most one round file and only when not compact (`overlap_report` sits behind `!IsCompact()` in internal/cli/audit_record.go, and `latestAuditRoundOverlapReport` in audit_overlap.go reads only the latest round), and `runAuditRecord` reads no prior round file at all. Under `--compact` — the driver's mode, and the mode of the gated `--status --check` a CI runs every round — the walk goes from zero round-file reads to O(history) reads. The only consumer that needs the exact count rather than "at least the threshold" is the `message` string: condition 1 is a `>=` test, and §2.2's stable-versus-just-repaired distinction is fully served by a count saturated one round above the threshold. An unbounded read is being spent on a display number.

finding: The rule added this round to close the open_roles-empty gap is defended by a claim the emitted string contradicts. §2.4 states: 'When every open row carries no role it is [] and unattributed_open equals other_roles_open; the object then names no lens, and message says so rather than leaving the empty array to be interpreted.' Its two forms differ only by the parenthetical suffix, so the all-unattributed state emits 'spec-coverage clean 2 rounds; 3 findings open from other roles (including 3 with no role, which may be spec-coverage''s)' — byte-identical in shape to the 3-of-24 partial case, and its main clause positively asserts the findings are open 'from other roles' at the exact moment open_roles is [] and no other role holds any. The sentence is the sole stated reason the [] value is safe under --compact, where §2.5 drops role_streaks and divergence is the only per-role surface left.

finding: §2.4 guards divergence on spec staleness (condition 3, engine.StateStale) and explains at length why a spec edited mid-streak is deliberately tolerated, but §2 never mentions the other staleness axis tp already measures and already reports on the same output: roles_stale (engine.RolesStale over the latest audit round's stored roles_hash, emitted by runAuditStatus). A streak of 9 clean spec-coverage rounds can span an auditor-corpus change — a re-eject, a focus override, a narrowed spec-coverage role — and the signal's whole claim is that "the panel has been stable long enough for the remaining findings to be backlog" (§2.2). §1's constraint is that a rule which could fail in two directions fails toward "keep auditing", and a corpus change mid-streak is exactly a measurable instability the streak silently spans. As written I have to decide unilaterally whether to add a roles_stale term, and either choice is defensible against the spec text.
